notes.decision: Standard Kephalaia running title 'Of the Teacher' (= ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲍ in glossary) here written with vowel ⲡⲉⲁⲍ for ⲡⲥⲁⲍ — a recognized scribal/dialectal variant.

The character + recurs throughout this page (lines 8, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 [ⲛⲥⲧ-], 24, 27, 28, 29) as an editorial mark in the transcription representing letters resolved contextually. In ⲯⲩⲭⲏ contexts (++ⲩⲭⲏ, +ⲩⲭⲏ) the second + represents ⲯ; preceding +-marks represent the genitive ⲛ̄ or article ⲧ-/ⲡ-. In line 18 ϣⲁⲩ+ⲟⲩⲱ resolves to ϣⲁⲩⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'they habitually raise' (per terminology rule, ⲧⲟⲩⲱ MUST be 'raise' preserving vertical-soteriological semantics). I preserve + literally in the Coptic field and translate based on resolved context.

Lexeme of uncertain identity. Likely Greek loanword μνεία/μνῆσις 'remembrance' or μνήστωρ-class word, or perhaps the end of a damaged compound. Given the chapter's central theme is ⲣ̄ⲡⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'making remembrance' for the deceased catechumen (lines 15, 17), 'remembrance' fits — possibly closing a previous chapter heading or transitioning into the dialogue. Left untranslated to flag uncertainty.

Translated 'in diminishment' rather than 'to diminish.' ⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲟ̄ⲉ = ⲧⲗⲁⲓ̈ⲟ̄ⲉ 'lessening, diminishing' (in glossary) used substantivally with ⲛ̄- as 'in (a state of) diminishment.' Recurs in lines 20, 27 within the cosmic-soteriological framework: the 'other soul' is in diminishment (= captive in sin/body), and the living soul is broadened through the diminishment of the other.

Contracted form of ⲡⲉϩϣⲃⲣ-ⲥⲩⲅⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'his fellow-kinsman' (attested fully in line 2 as ⲡⲉϩϣ[ⲃⲣ]ⲥⲩⲣⲣⲉ[ⲛ]ⲏⲥ). The shortened -ⲉⲛⲟⲥ form appears at lines 9-10 and likely also in segments 5-6. Same referent: the kinsman-soul that intercedes for a captive man, paralleling the Living Soul that intercedes for the catechumen.

The macron-marked ⲡⲣⲉ̄ at line 21 end is ambiguous. Best candidates: (a) ⲡⲣⲏ 'the sun' — fits Manichaean cosmology (light-soul redeemed via sun-ship); (b) ⲡⲣⲉⲛ 'the name' — fits 'redeem in the name of this man.' The continuation [ⲙ]ⲡⲓⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'of this man' on line 22 favors (b). Translated tentatively as 'within the ⲡⲣⲉ̄ of this man'; the precise referent (sun / name / seed) requires parallels.

Verbal form taking ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ 'a substance' as object. Tentative reading as Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲣϥ̄/ϩⲱⲣϣ̄ 'spread out, scatter forth' or related distributive verb. Translated 'scatter-forth' provisionally; alternative readings include 'gather' (cf. ⲉⲉⲥⲧϥ̄ in vocabulary) or 'fashion.' The cosmological-soteriological context — the redeeming soul providing/distributing substance to the released catechumen — fits a distributive sense.

Reading ⲁⲣⲁⲧⲏ as ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ⲏ 'at his feet' (cf. ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in glossary, and accumulated ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'at their feet'). With ϣⲁⲣⲁϩ = ϣⲁⲣⲟϥ 'to/with him' the phrase suggests the living-relative 'stands at his (the deceased's) feet' (i.e., approaches the Elect on his behalf) and causes the church to make remembrance. Idiomatic for petitioning supervisory presence.
